title: A Portrait for the Choir
premise: When Lior Voss returns to the decaying coastal town of Greywater to bury his twin sister Noa, he discovers every photograph in their grandmother's house now contains an empty chair that wasn't there before — and the chair is slowly filling with something only he can see. The town's choir, a found family of misfits who have guarded a secret since 1974, confesses that they took something from the drowned church that year: a portrait that keeps its subjects alive by feeding them borrowed years. Noa's death was the debt coming due. To save what remains of his family and free the town, Lior must return the portrait to the church before the tide turns on the winter solstice — but returning it means choosing which memories of Noa he is willing to lose. In the end, Lior gives the portrait back at terrible cost, the choir sings it home, and he stays in Greywater not as a believer but as a keeper, learning that loyalty sometimes means carrying truths no court would ever recognize.
about_author: Xanthe Amberdale is the pen name of a former church archivist who spent a decade cataloguing parish records in drowned coastal towns before turning to fiction. They write horror about inheritance, small communities, and the debts families refuse to name aloud.

chapters.title: The Wrong Grave
chapters.summary: Lior arrives in Greywater for Noa's funeral and finds the headstone already weathered, as if she'd been dead for decades. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: disorientation and grief curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: House of Extra Rooms
chapters.summary: Clearing grandma's house, Lior counts eleven rooms where the blueprints say ten. He hears humming from behind a wall. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: unease sharpening into dread.

chapters.title: The Chair in Every Photograph
chapters.summary: Every family photo, dating back to 1974, now includes an empty wooden chair. In the oldest one, someone is almost sitting in it. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: rational mind beginning to crack.

chapters.title: The Choir Practice Nobody Announces
chapters.summary: Following the humming, Lior finds six strangers rehearsing in the flooded chapel basement — people who greet him by name. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: wary curiosity; first contact with the choir.

chapters.title: Maren Keeps the Ledger
chapters.summary: Choir leader Maren Ash shows Lior a ledger of names and dates; Noa's entry was closed three weeks early. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: guilt worn like a uniform.

chapters.title: What Was Taken in 1974
chapters.summary: Maren recounts how the original choir stole a portrait from the drowning church to save their dying members — and how it has demanded repayment ever since. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: confession as relief and terror.

chapters.title: Noa's Last Voicemail
chapters.summary: Lior replays Noa's final message: 'It's sitting in your chair now.' He realizes she came here first. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into purpose.

chapters.title: The Portrait That Isn't Hung
chapters.summary: In the sealed attic, Lior finds the portrait wrapped in sailcloth — six faces painted on it, all still breathing faintly. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: awe tipping into violation.

chapters.title: Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Choir member Tobias, 90 and hale, explains the bargain: the portrait lends life, but the ledger collects. POV: Tobias. Emotional beat: complicity without apology.

chapters.title: The Town That Looks Away
chapters.summary: Lior questions neighbors; everyone knows, no one speaks. A shopkeeper sells him salt and says 'for the threshold.' POV: Lior. Emotional beat: isolation — justice here has no courtroom.

chapters.title: First Debt Called
chapters.summary: Choir member Ilsa collapses, aged decades overnight; her ledger line burns black. The chair in the photographs gains an occupant. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: fear made flesh.

chapters.title: Rules of the House
chapters.summary: Grandma's journal surfaces: never sing after dark, never count the rooms twice, never let it learn your face. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: grim education; agency forming.

chapters.title: The Face It Learned
chapters.summary: The newest figure in the portrait has Noa's profile. Lior smashes a mirror rather than see his own beside hers. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: horror becoming personal.

chapters.title: Maren's Original Sin
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Maren's POV, 1974: young Maren carried the portrait out of the flooding church while the organist sang against the water. Emotional beat: the founding wound.

chapters.title: Solstice Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Tobias calculates the tide tables: the portrait can be returned only when the drowned chapel rises, at winter solstice — nineteen days away. POV: Tobias. Emotional beat: a clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: Recruiting the Skeptic
chapters.summary: The choir formally asks Lior to carry the portrait back; only kin of the debtor can return it. He refuses. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: anger at being conscripted by other people's sins.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Ilsa dies singing. At the funeral, half the town mouths the hymn from memory. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: communal complicity exposed.

chapters.title: The Room That Counts Twelve
chapters.summary: The house grows a twelfth room containing Noa's childhood bedroom, perfectly preserved, dust-free. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: temptation — the house offers comfort as bait.

chapters.title: A Night Inside the Portrait
chapters.summary: Lior dreams himself into the painting: six figures at a table, one seat open, Noa's voice asking him to sit. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: longing versus survival.

chapters.title: The Organist's Descendant
chapters.summary: Lior tracks down Ruth, granddaughter of the 1974 organist who sang against the flood — the only person the portrait fears. POV: Ruth. Emotional beat: hope with sharp edges.

chapters.title: Ruth's Refusal
chapters.summary: Ruth wants the whole choir punished, not saved; she'll help only if Lior lets the singers pay. POV: Ruth. Emotional beat: justice versus mercy, stated plainly.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Someone burns the boathouse where the sailcloth and ritual records are kept. Suspicion splits the choir. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: trust fracturing under pressure.

chapters.title: Tobias Confesses
chapters.summary: Tobias admits he burned nothing but reveals who did: the shopkeeper, whose father drowned in '74 and whose grief the portrait feeds on. POV: Tobias. Emotional beat: pity for the antagonist.

chapters.title: The Shopkeeper's Bargain
chapters.summary: The shopkeeper offers Lior a deal: give him the portrait, and Noa comes back — the portrait can give back what it took. POV: shopkeeper (Hollis). Emotional beat: the devil's offer, sincerely meant.

chapters.title: Noa at the Door
chapters.summary: Something wearing Noa's voice knocks at midnight, reciting childhood secrets only Noa knew. Lior nearly opens it. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: the cost of wanting truth over comfort.

chapters.title: Ledger Audit
chapters.summary: Maren opens the full ledger: forty names across fifty years, most of them townsfolk who never joined the choir. Everyone ate from the stolen table. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: collective guilt, no clean hands.

chapters.title: Ruth Changes Terms
chapters.summary: After hearing the ledger read aloud, Ruth agrees to help — if the choir sings the portrait home themselves, facing it, not hiding behind Lior. POV: Ruth. Emotional beat: justice reframed as accountability.

chapters.title: Rehearsal for the Drowned
chapters.summary: The choir practices the organist's counter-hymn from Ruth's recovered notation; each verse costs the singer a memory. POV: multiple choir members. Emotional beat: sacrifice rehearsed in daylight.

chapters.title: What Maren Forgets First
chapters.summary: Maren loses her memory of 1974 itself — the founding sin — and must decide whether to keep singing without knowing why. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth made literal.

chapters.title: Hollis Takes the Chapel
chapters.summary: Hollis locks the choir out of the chapel basement and begins his own rite to bind the portrait to himself and raise Noa. POV: Hollis. Emotional beat: grief turned tyrant.

chapters.title: The Tide Turns Early
chapters.summary: Anomalous tides flood the low streets; the solstice window will close in two days, not nineteen. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: panic, plans collapsing.

chapters.title: Breaking Into the Drowned Church
chapters.summary: Lior, Ruth, and what's left of the choir breach the flooded chapel through the old crypt at low tide. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: descent — literal and moral.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Font
chapters.summary: They find Hollis mid-rite, the portrait unveiled, Noa's shape condensing above the font. Lior must choose between the rite and the hymn. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: climax of competing loyalties.

chapters.title: The Counter-Hymn
chapters.summary: The choir sings against Hollis's rite, losing memories verse by verse; Maren sings blind, not knowing why, and it holds. POV: Maren. Emotional beat: transcendence through shared cost.

chapters.title: Returning What Was Taken
chapters.summary: Lior carries the portrait into the rising water and hangs it on the drowned wall; the painted figures exhale fifty borrowed years at once. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: restitution as release.

chapters.title: The Price of the Picture
chapters.summary: The debt settles: Tobias ages gently and dies content; the house shrinks back to ten rooms; Noa's presence fades from the photos — and from Lior's sharpest memories of her. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: grief accepted rather than cheated.

chapters.title: Hollis at the Waterline
chapters.summary: Hollis, refused his miracle, wades into the channel; the town pulls him out and, for the first time, sits with his grief instead of looking away. POV: Hollis. Emotional beat: justice outside the law becomes mercy.

chapters.title: Eleven Chairs, All Empty
chapters.summary: Weeks later, the photographs show ordinary rooms again. Lior finds one last image: the choir table, eleven chairs, all empty, all waiting. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: quiet, watchful peace.

chapters.title: The New Archivist
chapters.summary: Lior takes over grandma's journal and the ledger, becoming keeper of Greywater's true history — the record no official archive would hold. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: vocation born from loss.

chapters.title: A Portrait for the Choir
chapters.summary: On the solstice anniversary, the choir sings in the restored chapel; Lior listens from the back, a skeptic who keeps the faith of others safe. Somewhere in the paint, faintly, someone hums along. POV: Lior. Emotional beat: belonging without belief — the found family endures.
